standard_prerequisites.name: Random index sequence
standard_prerequisites.statement: Independent uniform indices i_1, i_2, ... and L the first index at which the set of indices seen equals the whole coordinate set.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the randomness driving the scan.

standard_prerequisites.name: Contraction rate
standard_prerequisites.statement: The same one minus delta over a linear function of n bound as for the systematic scan.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the bound asserted on an event.

standard_prerequisites.name: Certification in linear time
standard_prerequisites.statement: The event carries a certificate that can be checked in time linear in the number of indices.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the third assertion of the statement.

core_obligations: Define the indices recursively so that each coordinate is assigned the number of the last step at which an index at least as large as it was drawn, and express the random product as a product of blocks (source lines 580-591).
Apply the general spectral gap theorem to each block, so that the product of a full collection of blocks contracts by the stated rate (source line 591).
Show that the event that L is not much larger than n has the required probability, and exhibit the certificate: the drawn indices themselves, checked in linear time (source lines 592-628).

proof_roadmap.step: Rewrite the random product as a product of blocks and apply the general theorem.
Bound the probability of the event and describe the linear-time certificate.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled theorem at source lines 570-577: for a uniform independent sequence of coordinate indices, with L the first time all coordinates have been seen, there is an event of high probability on which the product of the corresponding matrices contracts by one minus delta over thirty-two n, and the event can be certified in linear time from the indices. The proof (source lines 579-628) does three things the statement does not display: it rewrites the random product as a product of deterministic blocks by a recursive assignment of indices, applies the general spectral gap theorem to each block, and then controls the number of blocks together with the certificate step. The statement records the contraction, the probability and the certification but none of the block decomposition.
